text:
The search results don't name a specific power station model, so I can't recommend a brand. They do show how to pick one by capacity (Wh) and heater wattage.

**What to look for**
- **Capacity in Wh matters most.** [Off Grid Power Boom](https://offgridpowerboom.com/reptile-heat-battery-backup/) says a portable power station usually beats a UPS for reptile heat. You need sustained watts for hours, not just a quick handoff. Pure-sine AC outlets can run the heat mat, ceramic heat emitter (CHE) clamp lamp, or thermostat strip you already own. Some units have UPS/pass-through modes, but transfer times vary by brand, so check the maker's page for the model you buy.
- **Size it to your heater.** [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage) estimates usable energy at about 85% of the rating, and the station itself draws roughly 5–20 W with AC on.
  - A 24 W heat mat plus the station's draw is about 40 W. A 288 Wh unit runs that for about 6–8 hours, and a 2,073.6 Wh unit for about two days.
  - A 100 W ceramic emitter on a thermostat at half duty averages about 50 W. A 2,073.6 Wh unit runs that for about a day.
- **These are calculations, not tests.** Dealectric says it found no measured reptile run on a power station. Off Grid Power Boom likewise says it didn't run an enclosure overnight. Both are also selling or earning commissions, so treat the figures as estimates and leave yourself a margin.

**Which size to pick**
- For a small enclosure with a heat mat, a station of roughly 300 Wh covers a typical overnight outage.
- For a CHE or a longer outage, aim for about 2,000 Wh.
- A thermostat on the heater lowers the average draw.

**Backups that cost less or last longer**
- Many reptiles tolerate a short outage with no power. Dealectric cites one vet's guidance of about a day at 65 °F for bearded dragons. Cover the enclosure with blankets and keep the room door shut.
- [Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-reptile-during-a-power-outage) suggests chemical hand warmers and warm water bottles wrapped in towels. It also says a home generator can power your regular heating equipment.
- A [Reddit commenter](https://www.reddit.com/r/reptiles/comments/1qahs27/we_had_to_get_creative_during_a_power_outage_and/) uses an XL power bank for a lamp and shipping heaters (large hand warmers) that last up to 3 days.
- Hatchlings, juveniles, sick animals and tropical species are more vulnerable, and chameleons have a much shorter window, so prioritize them ([Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage)).

If you tell me your species, heater type and wattage, and how long an outage you want to cover, I can work out the Wh you need. I'd need a new search to name specific models.
